entities.name: Petersen Automotive Museum
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Petersen Automotive Museum, located in Los Angeles, California, stands as a premier institution dedicated to the preservation and exhibition of automotive history. Founded in 1994 by Robert Petersen, the museum occupies a 300,000 square foot building on Wilshire Boulevard and houses an extensive collection of over 300 automobiles. The museum's significance lies not only in its impressive collection but also in its role as a cultural touchstone for the automotive community, influencing car enthusiasts and collectors worldwide. It serves as a hub for educational programming, exhibitions, and events that highlight the impact of the automobile on American culture and global society.

The museum’s collection spans over a century, showcasing vehicles from the early 20th century to contemporary models, including rare automobiles, vintage racing cars, and concept vehicles. Notable exhibits have included the “Hollywood Dream Cars” and “The Art of the Automobile,” which feature vehicles that have shaped the film industry and automotive design. The Petersen is also known for its innovative use of space, transforming the former department store into an engaging experience that draws in over 250,000 visitors annually, making it a vital institution in Los Angeles’s cultural landscape.

The legacy of the Petersen Automotive Museum extends beyond its walls, influencing the way automotive history is documented and appreciated. It has inspired numerous automotive museums across the globe, encouraging a greater understanding of the societal changes driven by automotive technology. The museum has also played a pivotal role in fostering a community of car lovers and historians, bridging generational gaps in automotive appreciation and knowledge. By emphasizing the artistic and historical significance of automobiles, the museum has contributed to a broader conversation about technology and culture, exemplifying how the automotive industry has shaped modern life.
